verdict.headline: Ross Stores' blowout Q2 rescues the retail read ahead of Nvidia's print and Jackson Hole
verdict.label: HOLD — 0 of 3 regime indicators active: 30Y 5.24% (below 5.40%); Brent $93 (below $94 gate); BTC $77.7K (above $62K floor). ROST +7.92% AH on comps +10%, EPS $2.66 vs $1.94 est — retail scorecard flips 3-1 (HD, TGT, ROST beat; WMT miss); Nasdaq futures +0.5%; NVDA T-5 days to Aug 26 print; Warsh Jackson Hole keynote Aug 28.
verdict.rationale_short: Ross Stores reversed Thursday's WMT shock with a decisive Q2 beat — comparable-store sales +10% (second consecutive double-digit quarter), EPS $2.66 vs $1.94 consensus, revenue $6.3B vs $6.15B, gross margin +625bps. IEEPA tariff refunds contributed ~$253M (~$0.60/share), but +10% comps on record traffic are not a refund artifact; off-price retail is capturing a structural consumer trade-down that WMT, anchored on everyday need, cannot access. The retail scorecard flips to 3-1: HD (+1.7% comps), TGT (+3.8%), ROST (+10%) all beat; WMT's 2.6% Q2 miss and Q3 EPS guide ($0.62-$0.64 vs $0.73 consensus) now reads as format-specific demand response, not systemic consumer deceleration. BTC extended to $77.7K (from $73.9K AH Thursday) on continuing Clarity Act momentum. The regime picture is intact: 0 of 3 indicators active. HOLD posture is maintained — ROST's beat validates the 'selective consumer' read and strengthens the AI-demand backdrop entering NVDA's Aug 26 print, but the NVDA/Jackson Hole 36-hour window (NVDA Aug 26 AH, Warsh keynote Aug 28) concentrates the most directional repricing risk of the quarter into a single week. Adding equity exposure into both events simultaneously is taking uncompensated binary risk at limited upside vs. current levels.

trade_setups.asset: ROST — off-price trade-down proxy at new structural level
trade_setups.thesis: ROST's +10% comps on record traffic (second consecutive double-digit quarter) confirms the consumer trade-down thesis in the strongest possible terms. The $0.60/share IEEPA refund is real but does not explain traffic-driven volume: off-price retail is capturing incremental spend from consumers who are trading down in format (off-price vs. department store, vs. WMT general merchandise) rather than reducing spending. ROST's 3-for-3 earnings consistency this year makes it the highest-conviction consumer discretionary idea heading into Q3. The risk to this thesis is the tariff refund being one-time, not structural — but even ex-refund, ROST's comps would be $0.60/share lower, implying normalized Q2 EPS near $2.06 — still above the $1.94 estimate on comp momentum alone.
trade_setups.entry: ROST AH $247.12. Consolidation above $245 through Friday's close confirms a structural re-rating. Pullbacks to $235-240 on broader market weakness (e.g., 10Y above 4.75%) are the preferred entry for a position held into Q3 October earnings. $240 is the new line to hold above.
trade_setups.invalidation: ROST opens below $235 on broad retail sector de-rating driven by a WMT demand-softening narrative that overrides the off-price separation trade; or tariff refund one-time nature dominates consensus into the close.
trade_setups.horizon: 4-6 weeks; Q3 October earnings is the next catalyst.

bear_case: Ross Stores' IEEPA tariff refunds account for ~$0.60 of the Q2 EPS beat — a one-time benefit with no confirmed continuation into H2. Ex-refunds, FY EPS is $8.01-$8.17, a material restatement of the full-year trajectory. Separately, the +10% comp thesis requires a consumer who is actively trading down; if WMT management's Q3 guidance proves conservative (tariff cost timing, not structural demand softening) and WMT comps recover to 3-4%, the trade-down thesis partially unwinds and ROST's premium multiple compresses. Macro risk: the 30Y at 5.24% is 16bps from the 5.40% regime trigger; Brent at $93 is $1 from the $94 gate; both pressures are Iran-driven (Hormuz stalemate, eight vessel attacks in August) and can move abruptly on geopolitical events. VIX at 15.20 (above Thursday's 14.89 close despite positive futures) suggests investors are bidding event protection for NVDA and Jackson Hole rather than selling it — options pricing is acknowledging the binary risk even as index futures imply calm. Level that changes the constructive read: ROST consolidates above $245 through today's close, AMD reclaims $484, 30Y holds below 5.20%, and Brent pulls back below $91 on a Hormuz de-escalation signal — all four simultaneously.
